lessons.title: Chapter 2 — The close checklist
lessons.html:
The close runs from one checklist: nine lines, each with a named owner, in order — later lines verify earlier ones.

1. Cut-off sweep. The month's documents in: draft documents submitted or cancelled, the Delivered Items To Be Billed and Received Items To Be Billed reports read in naira, known latecomers accrued. Chapter 3 covers the reports.

2. The manual layer. The recurring set runs — the Auto Repeat entries confirmed fired, the template journals posted (accruals, prepayment consumptions, the salary posting, depreciation where not yet automated); accrual reversals confirmed (the Reverse Journal Entry pairs); the month's journal review from the filtered Journal Entry list — the five questions, the count.

3. The sweeps. Suspense to zero, each item classified. The unaddressed check — the ledger filtered to the Company's default cost centre — at or near zero (module 6). Floating payments and credits cleared in Payment Reconciliation (module 4).

4. The reconciliations. Every bank matched in the Bank Reconciliation Tool; the Bank Reconciliation Statement saved per account; cash counts current (module 3).

5. The bridges. Stock ledger to stock accounts. Sales Register and Purchase Register tax totals to the tax accounts' GL movements (module 5's pre-filing gate, run whether or not a filing falls this week). Trial Balance controls to the Accounts Receivable and Payable report totals (module 4's tie check).

6. Subsidiary outputs collected. The AR/AP routine's artifacts, the tax cycles' zero checks, the stock month-end outputs — collected, not re-performed.

7. The Trial Balance scan. Module 1's ten minutes: should-be-zero accounts with balances (Stock Received But Not Billed aging, suspense residents, the Round Off account trending), wrong-side balances, unrecognised lines — each opened in the General Ledger report.

8. The freeze advance. Only after lines 1-7: Accounts Frozen Upto advanced to the month's end date, the stock freeze with it, the advance noted in the close log. The order is fixed — sweep first, freeze second; a close that freezes first manufactures its own next-month stragglers.

9. Statements produced and read. The three reports run from the sealed month, the twenty-minute management reading held (Chapters 4-6), and the close bundle filed: the signed checklist, the reconciliation statements, the bridge confirmations, the reports — one folder per month.

Practical rules: one owner for the checklist, a named owner per line, lines 1-8 in days one to four, line 9 on day five. A line that keeps slipping is a process fault to fix, not a person to blame.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — Cut-off and its reports
lessons.html:
Cut-off is the rule that a month contains exactly its own documents. Its failures move real margin between months through omission alone, and the system has reports built for catching them.

The completeness pairs, with their reports.

• Deliveries and their invoices. Revenue books at the Sales Invoice; COGS books at the Delivery Note. A month whose deliveries posted but whose invoices lagged carries cost without revenue. The report: Delivered Items To Be Billed (Accounting or Selling reports) — every delivery awaiting its invoice, in naira. At close, the queue is either billed or carried knowingly with a note.
• Receipts and their bills. The mirror report: Received Items To Be Billed. The accounting side is handled by design — the Purchase Receipt credits Stock Received But Not Billed, so the liability accrues whether or not the supplier's invoice arrived. The close's job is the SRBNB age read: an old, large balance on that account means purchase invoices are not being processed.
• Consumptions and their accruals. Utilities consumed but unbilled, services received but uninvoiced — covered by the accrual templates in checklist line 2 (module 2's estimate → Reverse Journal Entry → actual rhythm).

The document sweep, step by step.

1. For each transaction doctype (Sales Invoice, Delivery Note, Purchase Receipt, Purchase Invoice, Payment Entry, Stock Entry, Journal Entry), open the list view filtered to Status = Draft and dated this month. This five-minute pass finds most stragglers — submit or cancel each one.
2. Read the two To-Be-Billed reports and act on them.
3. Accrue the known latecomers — the supplier who always bills on the 5th for the prior month gets a template accrual, reversed on arrival.
4. Run the sweep on day one of the close, so stragglers post with honest in-period dates before the freeze advances.

Worked example — why one document swings two months. A ₦500,000 delivery posts on the 30th; its invoice posts on the 2nd. Month one records ₦380,000 of COGS with no revenue: margin understated by ₦120,000. Month two records ₦500,000 of revenue with no COGS: margin overstated by ₦120,000. One late invoice, two distorted months in opposite directions — and for this reason a gross margin that swings on stable trade points first to cut-off, and why the To-Be-Billed reports are read at every close.

Summary. Check the pairs with their reports — Delivered Items To Be Billed, Received Items To Be Billed, the SRBNB age; sweep drafts by list view on day one; accrue the latecomers; freeze only after.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — Reading the Profit and Loss Statement
lessons.html:
Open Accounting > Financial Statements > Profit and Loss Statement. Set Company, the period, and Periodicity = Monthly with several months of columns — the trend view is the report's most useful shape. This chapter is the structure, the reading method, and the pre-reading checks.

The structure, top to bottom.

• Income — the period's invoiced trade, net of returns and credit notes.
• Cost of Goods Sold — the delivered goods' valuation, summed from the stock postings.
• Gross Profit — read with its percentage: the trading engine's health in one number, and the first line every reader checks.
• Expenses — grouped as the chart's design intended them to be read (module 1's reading test yielding returns monthly).
• Net Profit — after finance costs, exceptional items (labelled as exceptional — one blended into operations distorts every trend), and the business's own tax charge.

The reading method — four rules, in order.

1. Trend before level. Run with monthly columns and read this month against the last six. A gross margin that moved from 24% to 21% over a quarter is a finding regardless of whether 21% is acceptable.
2. Rate before naira. Margins and expense ratios compare across months of different sizes; raw naira mislead.
3. Decompose before concluding. A falling margin splits three ways — price, mix, or cost — with three different owners. Re-run the report filtered by Cost Center (and by the line dimension where module 6 added one): margin by branch and by line shows which component moved.
4. Drill before disputing. Click any figure: the report opens the General Ledger behind it, and the vouchers are two more clicks away. The disputed expense is opened live in the meeting, not argued from the page.

The pre-reading checks. Before trusting the figures, confirm the month's disciplines held:

• Cut-off — the To-Be-Billed reports were read (Chapter 3); the usual cause of a bouncing margin.
• Valuation — a COGS jump traced to a bad incoming rate; check the item's rate history.
• Accruals — the "cheap" month that simply has not been billed yet (line 2 ran).
• The unaddressed check — branch reads distorted by blank cost centres (module 6).
• Exceptional labelling — one-offs marked as one-offs.

The management reading. Twenty minutes, monthly, on a fixed day: the three-number headline (revenue, gross margin percentage, net profit), the trend columns, the material variances with one-line causes, and any decision the figures require. A standing meeting, not an email.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — Reading the Balance Sheet
lessons.html:
Open Accounting > Financial Statements > Balance Sheet as at the sealed date. The total always balances — the posting engine guarantees it — so the reading is line by line: every line is a claim, and every claim has a check performed elsewhere in this track.

The line checks.

• Fixed assets — cost less accumulated depreciation, agreeing with the Asset module's register (Chapter 7); the last physical verification current.
• Stock — the stock-to-accounts bridge agreed at close; the valuation honest; the dead-stock and aging reads qualifying how good the asset is beyond how big.
• Debtors — gross less the Provision for Doubtful Debts, shown rather than hidden; the tie check agreed (Trial Balance control = Accounts Receivable report total); the aging supporting the provision (module 4's matrix).
• Prepayments and supplier advances — the Prepaid Rent consuming on its Auto Repeat schedule; the supplier advances aged against expected deliveries, clean of items past plausibility.
• WHT Receivable — certificated or under active chase; the asset is only as real as its certificate file (module 5).
• Bank and cash — every balance matched in the Bank Reconciliation Tool this month, the Bank Reconciliation Statements in the close bundle, the floats counted.
• Creditors — tied to the Accounts Payable report; the SRBNB age read; supplier statements reconciled for the top names.
• Customer advances and accrued expenses — reported un-netted, each with its schedule; these liabilities are what keep the P&L honest.
• Tax custodies — at their explainable levels (post-remittance zero or the stated carry-forward), the reserve funded to match (module 5).
• Equity — retained earnings moves only through the Period Closing Voucher (Chapter 8) and governed distributions. An unexplained equity movement is a serious finding: deleted documents, forced balances, and migration errors all surface in equity, because equity is the residual where broken books hide. Chapter 9's Pattern 5.

The monthly balance-sheet read, as a procedure.

1. Run the report beside last month's (Periodicity = Monthly, two columns).
2. Read the working-capital lines against last month — stock, debtors, creditors; Chapter 6 restates these movements as cash.
3. Confirm the custody levels and the equity line unchanged except by known events.
4. Any line whose check failed is worked before the statements circulate, or circulated with an explicit note — never silently.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — Reading the Cash Flow statement
lessons.html:
Open Accounting > Financial Statements > Cash Flow. This report reconciles two facts that regularly diverge: the P&L shows a profit while the bank falls, or the reverse. Most trading businesses never read theirs.

Why profit and cash differ. Profit records earnings — a submitted Sales Invoice is revenue whether or not the customer has paid. Cash records movements. The gap is the balance sheet moving:

• Profit that became stock — margin sitting in the warehouse.
• Profit that became debtors — margin sitting in unpaid invoices.
• Profit consumed by paying creditors down.
• Profit spent on assets — the cold room capitalised to the balance sheet, not expensed.

A profitable business can run out of cash; a cash-rich business can be quietly unprofitable. The report starts from profit and shows, movement by movement, where the money went.

The three sections, as the report presents them.

1. Operating activities — profit adjusted for non-cash lines (depreciation added back: it consumed no cash) and the working-capital movements (stock up consumes cash; debtors up consumes cash; creditors up releases it). A healthy trading business generates positive operating cash most months. Chronically negative operating cash at a profitable business means the margin is being buried in stock and debtors faster than it is earned — the figure that explains why growth "doesn't feel like it".
2. Investing activities — the asset spend: the Chapter 7 capitalisations landing as outflows.
3. Financing activities — capital in, loans drawn and repaid, distributions out.

The three sections sum to the period's net cash movement, which agrees with the bank accounts' movement — already proven line by line in module 3's reconciliations.

The five-minute monthly read. The formal report exists; the working read is four questions:

1. Was operating cash positive — did the engine generate or consume?
2. Which working-capital line moved most, and why — one sentence per material movement, drilled from the Balance Sheet comparison?
3. What was invested, and was it planned?
4. What financed the difference, and is that source sustainable?

Practical rule: when the P&L and the bank app appear to disagree, do not argue from either — open the Cash Flow report. The answer is always one of the working-capital lines, and the report names which one moved.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — The Asset module: capitalisation to disposal
lessons.html:
Purchases that outlive their month — vehicles, generators, cold rooms, fit-outs — run through the Asset module, which maintains the register, computes depreciation, and posts it automatically.

Setup — the Asset Category. Open Assets > Asset Category > New: name the class (Vehicles, Plant, Fit-outs), set its accounts per company (Fixed Asset account, Accumulated Depreciation, Depreciation Expense), and its depreciation defaults — method (Straight Line is the trading business's standard), total number of depreciations, and frequency in months. The category is the policy carrier; individual assets inherit it.

The capitalisation policy. Written, with a value threshold: below it, expense regardless — a ₦40,000 printer is not worth an asset record's lifetime of administration. Above it, capitalise into the category list. The threshold is policy, not mood: expensing everything to dampen a good year, or capitalising to flatter a bad one, is the same abuse as moving a provision by discretion.

Creating assets from their documents. On the Item record, tick Is Fixed Asset and set the Asset Category. A Purchase Receipt or Purchase Invoice for that item then creates the Asset record automatically — the asset born from its purchase document, not reconstructed from a year-end spreadsheet. On the Asset record, confirm: gross purchase amount, Available-for-Use Date (depreciation starts here, not at the invoice date), location, and Cost Center — so depreciation lands on the branch that uses the asset. Submitting the Asset generates its depreciation schedule — the table of dates and amounts for its whole life.

Monthly depreciation. With Accounts Settings > Post Depreciation Entries Automatically enabled, the system posts each schedule row on its date: debit Depreciation Expense (addressed by the asset's cost centre), credit Accumulated Depreciation. The Balance Sheet carries cost less accumulated depreciation as net book value. Verify the posting once against the map; after that it is checklist line 2 confirming it fired.

Disposals. When an asset is sold or scrapped, use the Asset record's Sell / Scrap actions: selling creates the Sales Invoice against the asset (proceeds versus net book value, gain or loss posted); scrapping posts the write-off Journal Entry. Either way the Asset record's status closes with its date and evidence. An asset that physically left without a disposal entry leaves the register asserting property the business no longer holds. Location moves between branches are recorded with Asset Movement.

The annual verification. Run the Fixed Asset Register report and physically verify it once a year — each asset sighted or its absence resolved through the disposal flow, locations and cost centres corrected, the verification signed and filed. The Balance Sheet's fixed-asset line is only as reliable as the last verification.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Year-end, the audit, and the HealthTrade case
lessons.html:
Year-end is the twelfth monthly close plus a short annual list. This chapter covers the mechanics, the audit, and HealthTrade's close year.

The year-end additions.

1. The Period Closing Voucher. Open Accounting > Period Closing Voucher > New: select the fiscal year, the closing account (Retained Earnings), and the closing cost centre, and submit. The voucher closes every P&L account to retained earnings in one governed posting — the year's result becoming equity's newest layer, and the only routine way retained earnings ever moves.
2. The Fiscal Year. The next year created at least two months early (Accounting > Fiscal Year — module 8 covers the doctype), so the January 1st document never finds its year missing.
3. The annual layer landing together, scheduled across weeks: the full stock count, the Fixed Asset Register verification (Chapter 7), the chart and settings walks, module 5's annual returns.
4. The audit file — for a monthly-closing business, the year's twelve close bundles plus the annual artifacts, assembled by collation rather than creation.

The external audit, met. The interim walk-through tests the system of control — the tie, the bridges, the reconciliations, the separations — and a business that passes earns sampling instead of full substantive testing, which is the audit-fee conversation in one sentence. Fieldwork drills samples to documents (the drill-down performing for its most demanding audience). Confirmations arrive pre-answered by module 4's hygiene. The auditor's proposed adjustments — there will be some — are agreed or contested professionally by the accountant and booked by module 2's rules: referenced entries in the current or formally reopened period, never quiet edits, so the audited statements and the ledger end the season as the same document.

HealthTrade's close year. The first close takes four days of backlog: the draft sweep finds eleven stragglers across the doctypes, suspense empties (₦93,000 across six items), the To-Be-Billed reports are read for the first time, and the checklist runs to signature. Month two closes in two days. By month five the close lands on day three, and the statements are read at the day-five standing meeting. The readings produce decisions within the quarter: the Cash Flow read exposes the growth squeeze — positive profit, negative operating cash from stock build — which triggers the purchasing review; the P&L trend columns catch a two-point margin slide, decomposed by cost centre to one branch's discounting; and the Balance Sheet walk retires the last unexplained line. At year-end: the Period Closing Voucher posts retained earnings' only movement of the year, the audit's walk-through passes on first presentation, fieldwork samples rather than excavates, and the three agreed adjustments book by the rules. The audit closes three weeks earlier than the prior year, at a lower fee, with the statements and the ledger identical.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes & the seventh law
lessons.html:
The close-and-statements layer's recurring failures, then the review list.

Pattern 1 — the never-closed month. Symptom: Accounts Frozen Upto blank or a year old; statement dates nobody trusts; every report a draft. Cause: the close never instituted (Chapters 1-2). Fix: the first close performed once with its backlog, then the checklist with named owners, the day-five target, and the freeze advance keeping each sealed month sealed.

Pattern 2 — the year-end backlog. Symptom: twelve months of accruals, reconciliations, and corrections processed in January; statements about a year nobody remembers. Cause: closing annually what should close monthly (Chapter 1). Fix: the monthly rhythm — the pattern disappears by construction.

Pattern 3 — the bouncing margin. Symptom: gross margin swinging month to month on stable trade; owners distrusting the P&L. Cause: cut-off noise read as news (Chapter 3). Fix: the day-one draft sweep, the Delivered and Received Items To Be Billed reports read in naira at every close, the SRBNB age watched, and the ₦500,000 worked example taught to whoever reads the statements.

Pattern 4 — statements produced but not read. Symptom: the reports generated, circulated, filed — and no decision ever traced to them; the owner learning the business's position from the bank app. Cause: the reading habit never installed (Chapters 4-6). Fix: the twenty-minute monthly reading as a standing meeting, the four P&L rules, the balance-sheet line checks, the four cash-flow questions, and the three-number headline.

Pattern 5 — the unexplained equity movement. Symptom: retained earnings shifting between periods with no Period Closing Voucher behind it; equity used as a plug. Cause: the most serious failure here — history edited at its last hiding place (Chapters 5, 8): deleted documents, forced balances, migration errors, all washing up in equity. Fix: each movement traced in the General Ledger to its cause, the Period Closing Voucher restored as retained earnings' only routine mover, deletion rights removed (module 8's settings), and the equity line added to every monthly balance-sheet walk.

The review list. Before the quiz, confirm you can: state the five conditions of a closed month and where the freeze lives (Accounts Frozen Upto + the frozen-edit role); run the nine checklist lines in order and explain sweep-before-freeze; use the two To-Be-Billed reports and the SRBNB age read, and walk the ₦500,000 example; read the P&L with the four rules and the pre-reading checks; walk the Balance Sheet line checks and state the equity rule; answer the Cash Flow's four questions; set up an Asset Category, capitalise from a purchase document with Is Fixed Asset, enable automatic depreciation, and run a disposal; and post a Period Closing Voucher and assemble the audit file by collation.

The seventh law: the books close monthly, the statements are read monthly, and a sealed month stays sealed. Module 8 covers the settings, authorities, and calendar that hold the finance layer together.

advanced_accounts.title: Accounts 8 — Advanced Accounts: Settings, Controls & Structure
advanced_accounts.desc: The structural layer in ZhiftERP: the Accounts Settings walk (the freeze pair, unlink-on-cancellation, deletion, deferred accounting, rounding, Naming Series); Fiscal Years created ahead and the companies-follow-legal-reality rule with Is Internal Customer/Supplier inter-company invoicing; the four authorities separated in Role Permissions with the permission matrix; the finance calendar with Notifications; the handover and absence tests; the preventive/detective control map with the pairing principle and the CSA; and the professional boundaries — closing with the track's eight laws.

lessons.title: Chapter 1 — The Accounts Settings walk
lessons.html:
This final module covers the structural layer: the Accounts Settings, fiscal years and multiple companies, the separation of authorities in Role Permissions, the consolidated finance calendar, the handover test, the assembled control map, and the professional boundaries. It opens with the settings walk — performed with the accountant, each answer recorded, re-walked annually.

Open Accounts Settings and walk the fields that matter.

• Accounts Frozen Upto and Role Allowed to Set Frozen Accounts & Edit Frozen Entries — the period lock (module 7). Two health checks: a frozen date that never advances means the lock is not being used; a broadly granted edit role means the lock has no force. Grant the role to two named people at most.
• Unlink Payment on Cancellation of Invoice (and its sibling, Unlink Advance Payment on Cancellation of Order) — whether cancelling a document silently unlinks its payment allocations. The wrong value here quietly manufactures module 4's floating-payment backlog on its own. Decide it deliberately with the accountant and record the decision.
• Delete Accounting and Stock Ledger Entries on deletion of Transaction — controls what deletion is even capable of. Pair it with deletion rights kept off transaction doctypes for daily roles: module 7's equity pattern is largely made of deletions.
• Deferred accounting — Book Deferred Entries Based On and Automatically Process Deferred Accounting Entry: the automation of module 2's matching for item-driven deferred revenue and expense. Enable deliberately, wire its accounts, review its schedules like any template.
• Rounding and precision — currency precision consistent between documents and ledgers (a mismatch produces kobo-level reconciliation noise permanently), the Company's Round Off Account pointed at its designated leaf, and rounded-total behaviour set once.
• Credit control — the credit-limit machinery's master switches and the bypass role: who may override a blocked document. The gate numbers themselves live on the Customer records.
• Naming Series (Settings > Naming Series, for the financial doctypes) — chosen once with a long horizon: the invoice numbers on a filed VAT return must still make sense to an auditor in year seven. Never restarted, never reused.

The walk's three rules.

1. Each field is read as the policy question it is, and the answer is written in the implementation file.
2. Changes after go-live are governed events with a reason and a record — not toggles flipped per complaint.
3. The annual re-walk (Chapter 4's calendar) is the only routine occasion on which settings change.

lessons.title: Chapter 2 — Fiscal years and multiple companies
lessons.html:
Two structural mechanics: financial time is partitioned into Fiscal Years, and one site can hold several legal companies.

The Fiscal Year doctype. Open Accounting > Fiscal Year. Each record carries the year's start and end dates and the companies it applies to.

• Create the next year at least two months early. A January 2nd Sales Invoice that cannot submit because nobody created the year is the most avoidable start-of-year failure.
• Align to the statutory year — the calendar year for most Nigerian companies, but the doctype serves any twelve months; the accountant confirms.
• Close in sequence — one Period Closing Voucher per year (module 7).
• The Fiscal Year is also the Budget's container (module 6) and the axis of the comparative filters on every financial statement — trend reads depend on clean year boundaries.
• Backdating into a closed fiscal year changes audited, filed figures. The default answer is module 2's rule: correct in the current period, remarks naming the original date. Formal reopening is the accountant's rare, documented decision.

Multiple companies. The Company doctype supports several legal entities on one site: each with its own chart (or a shared template with per-company accounts), its own Fiscal Year list, its own defaults, its own separately sealed books — with group-level users able to report across.

The rule: companies follow legal reality, never reporting convenience. Separate registered entities keep separate books because the law treats them as separate persons — the audit, the tax filings, and the liability wall all run per entity. A branch is a Cost Center (module 6); a branch promoted to a Company because someone wanted "separate books" acquires statutory filing obligations to solve a reporting problem a cost centre solves at no cost.

Inter-company transactions, with the system's machinery. Where entities genuinely transact — management fees, recharges, stock moved, loans:

1. Mark the counterparties: on the Customer record, Is Internal Customer with its represented company; on the Supplier record, Is Internal Supplier. The system then offers Create Inter Company Invoice — the Sales Invoice in one entity generating the matching Purchase Invoice in the other, references mirrored automatically.
2. Reconcile the inter-company balances quarterly: entity A's receivable from B equals B's payable to A, to the kobo.
3. Pricing and tax treatment of inter-company charges are the accountant's and tax adviser's territory — set as policy before the first charge.

lessons.title: Chapter 3 — The four authorities in Role Permissions
lessons.html:
The finance layer has four distinct authorities, and the control design is keeping them in different hands. In the system, the separation is built in the Role Permission Manager and the submission Workflows.

The four authorities, as permissions.

1. Record — create/submit on the transaction doctypes. Trading documents broadly held; the Journal Entry pen narrowly held — module 2's two names, enforced as role permissions on the doctype.
2. Release — moving actual money: submit rights on the Payment Entry plus the bank-side mandate. Module 3's rule: the preparer of a run never releases it.
3. Close — sealing time: the Role Allowed to Set Frozen Accounts & Edit Frozen Entries (Chapter 1) and the Period Closing Voucher.
4. Configure — Accounts Settings, the Chart of Accounts, Cost Centers, dimensions, templates, Workflows: System Manager territory, the narrowest of all. Nobody's routine daily role includes it.

The rule: the authorities check each other only if they are held by different people. The recorder's entries are paid by someone else's release; the releaser's payments are checked by someone else's reconciliation; the closer's seal is read by someone else's review.

The pairings that must not collapse — what an audit tests first.

• The Journal Entry pen and Payment Entry release in different hands — one person holding both can write any entry and move any money.
• Payment preparer and releaser split — two people at any size.
• The reconciler is not the sole releaser — the mover of money is not its only checker.
• Adjustment powers narrow — the write-off workflow's two names (module 4), the journal Workflow's thresholds (module 2).
• The frozen-edit role disjoint from the daily recorders — the person posting today should not be able to repost yesterday's sealed figures.

Sizing. At eleven people, roles share heads: the founder releases what the accountant prepares; the accountant closes what the founder's review checks. The irreducible pairs survive any size because each is two people, not two departments — and where finance is one person, the owner is the second.

The permission matrix. One page: the four authorities mapped to named people, exported from the Role Permission Manager's assignments, reviewed annually and at every personnel change. The review's first question: does any one person hold more than one authority without a documented reason? Chapter 8 shows HealthTrade's answer.

lessons.title: Chapter 4 — The finance calendar
lessons.html:
The finance function runs on one consolidated calendar. Each line has a named owner and, where the system supports it, a Notification or Auto Repeat behind it so no line depends on memory. The calendar lives on the policy page and is reviewed annually.

Daily.

• The cash position: bank balances and the day's obligations — the Bank Account dashboard and the General Ledger by account.
• The exceptions scan: blocked documents, failed payments, till-session variances flagged overnight.
• Entry hygiene at the desks: references captured, cost centres cascading — the habits that keep every later routine cheap.

Weekly.

• The bank items sweep: new statement lines imported, charges booked through Create Voucher, deposits matched.
• The floating-payments glance: Payment Reconciliation at light cadence — items caught young allocate in minutes.
• The payment run cycle where one runs: prepared, evidenced, released by separated hands.

Monthly — the anchor.

• The close checklist (module 7's nine lines), days one to five, containing as collected inputs: the AR/AP routine (module 4's ninety minutes), the tax cycles with their zero checks (module 5), the journal review (module 2), the bank reconciliations (module 3), and the unaddressed check (module 6).
• The statements reading with management — the calendar's most important twenty minutes.
• The branch P&Ls issued and the Budget Variance Report read (module 6).

Quarterly.

• The provision review in depth — the matrix's judgments revisited (module 4).
• The correction log read by cause — upstream faults surfaced (module 2).
• The bank-charges read against the agreed schedule (module 3).
• The allocation pool audit — direct-first shrinking it (module 6).
• The advance agings' escalations resolved (module 4).
• Inter-company reconciliations where the structure exists (Chapter 2).

Annually — scheduled across weeks, not stacked.

• The Accounts Settings walk (Chapter 1) and the permission matrix review (Chapter 3).
• The chart walk — every account explainable in one sentence (module 1).
• The dimension audit (module 6) and the bank mandate review (module 3).
• The capitalisation policy review and the Fixed Asset Register verification (module 7).
• The budget build (module 6 — November) and the next Fiscal Year created (Chapter 2).
• The compliance calendar re-confirmed against current law (module 5).
• The year-end mechanics and the Period Closing Voucher (module 7).

Practical rule: a calendar line without a named owner will stop running. The annual review's first task is confirming every line still has one.

lessons.title: Chapter 5 — The finance handover test
lessons.html:
The handover test asks one question: could a competent newcomer, given only what is documented, run the finance function for a month with zero questions that only the departing person can answer? Finance — the function most often held in one trusted head — needs the test most.

The test, walked module by module. A finance function passes when:

1. The chart is documented — every account with its one-sentence purpose (module 1).
2. The journal governance is written: the pen's two names in Role Permissions, the template list, the correction rules (module 2).
3. The bank layer is documented: every Bank Account record with its purpose, every Mode of Payment mapping, the mandate — with last month's Bank Reconciliation Statements showing where each uncleared item stands (module 3).
4. The AR/AP routine's checklist and policy pages state the tie check, the provision matrix, and the write-off workflow (module 4).
5. The compliance calendar lists every obligation, day, authority, and evidence folder — with twelve months of folders showing the pattern (module 5).
6. The cost centre design is documented and the allocation policy answers every sharing question by pointing (module 6).
7. The close checklist states the month's nine lines, and the statement-reading method is written (module 7).
8. This module's calendar, permission matrix, and settings record hold the structure.

Every "no" identifies a module incompletely done. The documentation is not an extra deliverable — it is the by-product of each module done properly.

The absence test. The practical version: the key person takes uninterrupted leave, and the function runs on its calendar. What breaks during the absence is exactly what the documentation is missing. Run deliberately, it is the lowest-cost structural audit available, and its findings are fixed without a crisis.

The role path. A documented function makes progression legible: the bookkeeper (entries and desk hygiene) grows into the accountant (the close's owner, the journal pen's holder, the statements' first reader), who grows into the controller (the calendar's owner, the policies' custodian, the management reading's co-chair). Clean closes, young uncleared lists, and tied bridges are a promotion case written in numbers. The alternative — the whole function in one trusted head — is a single point of failure regardless of skill, and Chapter 9 treats it as one.

lessons.title: Chapter 6 — The control map: preventive and detective
lessons.html:
The track installed controls one module at a time. Assembled, they form a map with two families — and the assembly check is that every control in one family has a partner in the other.

Preventive controls — stop it before it posts.

• Separations: the four authorities in Role Permissions; the two-names patterns (journal pen, write-off, frozen-edit).
• Validations: mandatory Party on Receivable/Payable accounts; Mandatory For Profit and Loss on dimensions; the Journal Entry Difference field; the Stock-account fence.
• Fences: the frozen period (Accounts Frozen Upto); masters-not-messages for beneficiary changes; the forbidden journal list.
• Gates: Workflow approval thresholds; credit limits; Budget Stop actions on the governance account families.

Detective controls — catch what slipped through.

• Reconciliations: the Bank Reconciliation Tool monthly; the supplier-statement mirror.
• Ties: the control-to-report tie check; the register-to-account bridges; the custody zero check.
• Reviews: the monthly journal review; the Trial Balance scan; the audit-adjustments read.
• Aged reads: the uncleared-items list; the floating-payments list; the correction log by cause.

The pairing principle. Journal governance prevents; the journal review detects. The release separation prevents; the bank reconciliation detects. Mandatory dimensions prevent; the unaddressed check detects. A map with an unpaired fence has a blind spot — walk the map once and name each control's partner.

The fraud triangle, briefly. Fraud needs opportunity, pressure, and rationalisation. The business controls only opportunity, which is what the preventive family shrinks: the everything-role dismantled, custody segregated, the pen narrowed, the masters guarded. The detective family shortens time-to-discovery: what would compound for years surfaces at the month's reconciliation. The framing taught throughout removes the easiest rationalisation: controls protect the honest holder — the clean count and the documented approval are the honest person's own evidence.

The control self-assessment (CSA), annually.

1. List the controls by family, one page per control.
2. For each, name the evidence of its last execution: the reconciliation statement, the review sign-off, the Workflow approval log.
3. Read the tell-tale numbers: approval times (a second signature granted in seconds is not a review), uncleared ages, sweep sizes.
4. Revive or formally retire dead controls. A designed-but-dead control is worse than an absent one, because someone is relying on it.

lessons.title: Chapter 7 — Professional boundaries
lessons.html:
The finance layer is run alongside three professionals, and the boundaries must be held clearly — clients will blur them monthly.

The boundary map.

• The system role — the person who configures and operates ZhiftERP (this certification's territory) — owns the machinery: the configuration, the templates, the registers, the routines, the evidence structure, and the literacy to walk any entry with any professional as a peer. It does not make policy judgments.
• The accountant owns the policy: method choices, the provision matrix's percentages, the capitalisation threshold, recognition schedules, reopening decisions, and professional responsibility for the statements.
• The tax adviser owns the positions: rates, eligibility, reliefs, and stances where the law is unclear (module 5's boundary).
• The auditor owns the opinion: independent, sample-based, and best served by being served organised evidence (module 7's file).

The dividing sentence, worth memorising: the machinery makes the professionals' judgments executable and evidenced; it does not make the judgments.

The four working patterns.

1. The accountant co-designs from day one. The chart walk, the posting-map verification, the settings walk, and the policy pages are done with the accountant in the room. An accounts layer built without the accountant who must own it gets built twice.
2. Habit conflicts resolve by demonstration, not authority. Where the system's discipline conflicts with an accountant's established habit — the journal-habit case of module 2 is the standard example — the resolution is showing the document-first flow working and transferring the fluency, never deriding it.
3. The auditor is engaged early. The interim walk-through invited rather than endured, the close-bundle structure shared in advance, adjustments booked by the correction rules. A clean first year buys a lighter second — the relationship compounds like the authority relationship does.
4. The tax adviser is consulted before configuration. The new revenue stream's VAT treatment, inter-company pricing, and reform eligibility are settled before the templates are built. Reconfiguring after a wrong position costs far more than the consultation.

Summary. Machinery, policy, positions, opinion — four owners. Hold the boundary, co-design with the accountant, meet the auditor early, and loop the tax adviser in before configuring anything the law touches.

lessons.title: Chapter 8 — Case study: HealthTrade's structural year
lessons.html:
The structural layer, installed over four quarters. Every chapter appears.

Q1 — the settings walk (Chapters 1-2). The walk runs with the accountant, field by field, answers recorded. Accounts Frozen Upto is configured with the two-name edit role, and the freeze advance joins the close checklist. The Unlink Payment on Cancellation of Invoice setting is found at its wrong value — it had been silently unlinking allocations at every invoice cancellation, which explained part of module 4's original floating-payment backlog — and corrected, with the decision recorded. Naming Series are confirmed for the long term. The next Fiscal Year is created two months early, closing off the January failure before it can occur.

Q2 — the permission matrix (Chapter 3). The review exports the role assignments and finds the implementation-era all-permissions role still live on one user: the accountant, holding record, release, close, and configure "temporarily" since go-live. It is dismantled as a design exercise, not an accusation: Journal Entry create/submit narrowed to the accountant plus the named backstop, Payment Entry release moved to the founder (the founder releases what the accountant prepares), the frozen-edit role confirmed at two names, System Manager removed from daily use, and the matrix documented on one page. At the next audit, the walk-through passes its separation tests for the first time.

Q3 — the control self-assessment (Chapter 6). The first CSA walks the map by family and finds one designed-but-dead control: the second signature on large Journal Entries — live in the Workflow, rubber-stamped in practice, approvals landing in seconds, unread. It is revived with an evidence habit: the approver samples the entry's references before signing, and approval times are read quarterly from the Workflow log. The pairing walk confirms every fence has its detective partner, and the one-page-per-control file is started.

Q4 — the absence test (Chapter 5). The founder takes three uninterrupted weeks. Finance runs on its calendar: the close lands on day five without the founder's review, the payment runs release under the deputy-mandate design, and the compliance calendar's two in-window filings land on their days with their folders. The handover walk afterwards scores its first clean sheet — zero founder-only questions in the finance function. The MD's note in the year file: the business now runs on its documents in every function, including the one that counts them.

The year in numbers. Close: day five every month of H2. Audit: walk-through passed, three agreed adjustments, fee reduced. Floating payments: near zero every month since the unlink fix. Permission matrix: four authorities, no undocumented overlaps. Absence test: passed.

lessons.title: Chapter 9 — Common mistakes, the eighth law & the track's laws
lessons.html:
The structural layer's recurring failures, the module's law, and the track's eight laws assembled.

Pattern 1 — settings changed casually. Symptom: the frozen date never advancing; the unlink setting flipped per complaint; precision changed mid-year. Cause: Accounts Settings treated as toggles instead of policy (Chapter 1). Fix: settings behind the Configure authority, changes as governed events with a record, and the annual walk as the only routine occasion for change.

Pattern 2 — the everything-role. Symptom: one user holding record, release, close, and configure; the audit walk-through's first finding, every time. Cause: setup convenience never dismantled (Chapter 3). Fix: the four authorities separated in Role Permissions by the two-people patterns, the matrix documented and reviewed annually, and the dismantling run as a design exercise, not an accusation.

Pattern 3 — the branch promoted to a company. Symptom: statutory filings multiplying; inter-company balances nobody reconciles; "separate books" a Cost Center would have provided free. Cause: companies created for reporting convenience instead of legal reality (Chapter 2). Fix: cost centres for reading, Companies for legal persons, and the wrongly created entity wound down or made legally real with the accountant.

Pattern 4 — designed-but-dead controls. Symptom: reconciliations that quietly stopped; second signatures granted in seconds; checklist lines dropped. Cause: false assurance (Chapter 6) — worse than absence, because someone relies on the control. Fix: the annual CSA on evidence, the approval-time and uncleared-age numbers read, and dead controls revived or formally retired.

Pattern 5 — the single-person function. Symptom: finance running entirely in one trusted head; leave never taken; a close only one person can perform; an owner who cannot read the statements unaided. Cause: competence without structure (Chapter 5). Fix: the handover test as the standard, the documentation as each module's by-product, the role path making structure a promotion engine, and the absence test run deliberately.

The review list. Before the quiz, confirm you can: walk the Accounts Settings fields — the freeze pair, the unlink settings, deletion, deferred accounting, rounding, naming series — and state the three walk rules; create Fiscal Years ahead and state the companies-follow-legal-reality rule with the Is Internal Customer/Supplier machinery; map the four authorities in Role Permissions and name the pairings an audit tests; recite the calendar by frequency with its Notifications; run the handover and absence tests; walk the control map's two families with the pairing principle and the CSA; and state the four professional boundaries.

The eighth law: structure over individuals — authorities separated, settings governed, rhythms on the calendar, and the function passes the handover test.

The track's eight laws.

1. The books are written by documents, into a chart designed for reading.
2. The journal is the exception and the document is the rule — what a document can do, a document must do.
3. Every bank account is reconciled monthly, and every difference is named — never plugged.
4. The record is kept real, collectable, current and complete.
5. Tax money is held, not owned — reconciled, filed from the system, remitted from the reserve, and zeroed every cycle.
6. One chart, many readings — every posting carries its address, contribution decides, and allocation is written.
7. The books close monthly, the statements are read monthly, and a sealed month stays sealed.
8. Structure over individuals — authorities separated, settings governed, rhythms on the calendar, and the function passes the handover test.

This completes the Accounts Professional track.
